newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO view - H shares seen gaining from HK handover.
newsitem.headline: IPO view - H shares seen gaining from HK handover.

text.p: Hong Kong stock market investors, fired up by the territory's imminent return to China, are likely to focus this week on China-incorporated companies seeking a listing here, analysts said.

The market saw a record set last week with the Hong Kong initial public offering (IPO) of red chip Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, the Beijing municipal government-backed conglomerate. But with no immediate sign of other red chips coming on to the market, investor enthusiasm is likely to focus on H shares, analysts said.
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China. H shares are Hong Kong-listed shares of China-incorporated enterprises.
Analysts said investors were strongly attracted to China-linked companies with only a month to go before the handover of Hong Kong, ending more than 150 years of British rule.

"Investing spirit is still very high," said Patrick Cheng, corporate finance director at HSBC Investment Bank Asia. Red chip fever reached a pitch when Beijing Enterprises debuted on Thursday. The shares more than tripled from their initial price and finished the week at HK$45.20.
Beijing Enterprises was subscribed 1,276 times, smashing the record for over-subscription in Hong Kong.

Analysts noted that the company's price to earnings (P/E) ratio was about 67 times and said that the more affordably priced H shares offered investors an alternative. "The wave of demand for red chips is still there even though many have been trading at an unjustified P/E of 60 times," said Herbert Lau, analyst at Vickers Ballas.
"There is a lot of hot money around," Lau added. Among upcoming H shares, Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd is expected to issue 628.2 million shares ranging from HK$2.13 to HK$2.72 in a global flotation.
The company is raising funds to repay short-term debt and expand production facilities.
Its IPO is expected to run from June 2 to 5, and dealing in shares is expected to begin on June 12.
Agricultural tractor maker First Tractor Co Ltd is expected to raise HK$936 million to HK$1.19 billion by issuing 300 million H shares at a price ranging from HK$3.12 to HK$3.97 each.
Its Hong Kong IPO is expected to run from June 11 to 16 and trading is likely to begin on June 23.
Cheng said investors were taking a closer look at individual companies' fundamentals.
Toll road operator Jiangsu Expressway Co Ltd was expected to issue 1.2 billion H shares to raise about four billion yuan later in June, analysts said.
Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd is also expected to seek a listing later in 1997, raising capital to fund its expansion of resins and plastics production.

"Their IPOs will not be as strong as Beijing Enterprises. The response will depend on their own earnings prospects" and their links with Chinese authorities, said Eugene Law, director at Lippo Securities.
Lan Xue, associate director of SocGen-Crosby Securities, said the liquidity which had benefited red chips would flow over to H shares.
But some analysts have their doubts.
"I still have reservations on H shares because of the earnings disappointment by other listed Chinese enterprises," Law said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
